title: Physics-Refined Spatiotemporal Forecasting on Open-Boundary Hydrologic Graphs
abstract: arXiv:2610.01765v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Spatiotemporal forecasting on hydrologic graphs is especially prone to instability in open-boundary systems, where the forecast domain exchanges fluxes with an unobserved exterior. In such systems, boundary nodes receive external forcing, e.g., upstream inflows in rivers or tidal signals in coastal regions, that is typically unavailable at prediction time. The absence of this information can compound errors as forecasts unfold in an autoregressive fashion, leading to inferior long-horizon performance. This paper dissects this instability issue by exploring two questions. 1) What boundary forcing enters the forecast domain when information beyond the boundary is missing? 2) How should this forcing propagate through the domain without incurring error amplification under autoregressive rollout? tldr: 针对开边界水文系统中边界强迫信息缺失所导致的自回归预测误差累积问题，本文提出一种物理修正的计算框架，通过补偿缺失的边界强迫并设计其传播机制，实现无误差放大的长期稳定时空预测。
